subject: social_science

concepts.title: Multinational Corporation (MNC)
concepts.definition: A corporate enterprise that owns, manages, or regulates production activities in multiple countries rather than just its home country.
concepts.key_idea: Spreading production globally to secure cheap resources and minimize operational costs.
question_patterns: What is a multinational corporation?
Define an MNC and explain its primary objective.
How do multinational corporations organize their production globally?
Why do MNCs set up offices and factories in developing countries?
Explain how an MNC differs from a national company.

solution_steps.action: Identify the geographical scope of the company
solution_steps.explain: An MNC must own or control production facilities in more than one nation.
MNCs locate factories where cheap labor, raw materials, and favorable policies are available.

concepts.title: Foreign Investment
concepts.definition: Capital expenditure made by a multinational corporation to purchase assets such as land, buildings, and machinery in another country.
concepts.key_idea: Capital flows across borders with the expectation of earning profits from foreign assets.
question_patterns: What do you understand by foreign investment?
How is foreign investment different from regular domestic investment?
Why do multinational corporations make foreign investments?
In what ways do MNCs invest capital in local companies?
Explain the relationship between foreign investment and corporate profits.

solution_steps.action: Identify the source of the capital
solution_steps.explain: The investment must originate from an overseas entity, typically an MNC.
The funds are used to acquire productive assets like factories, land, or local businesses.

concepts.title: Total Production of a Multinational Plant
concepts.definition: The aggregate volume of goods manufactured by a multinational subsidiary, calculated by summing local market sales and export sales.
concepts.key_idea: Combining domestic and foreign market distributions to determine the total manufacturing output.
question_patterns: Calculate the total production of the factory given domestic and export sales.
What is the total output of a plant that sells some units locally and exports the rest?
Find the total number of units manufactured by adding local sales and exports.
Determine the total production volume of an MNC subsidiary.
How much total goods did the plant produce if exports were ... and domestic sales were ...?

solution_steps.action: Identify domestic sales and export sales
solution_steps.explain: Extract the values of domestic sales and export sales from the given problem.

concepts.title: Foreign Trade and Market Integration
concepts.section: FOREIGN TRADE AND INTEGRATION OF MARKETS
concepts.definition: The exchange of commodities and services across international borders, which connects distinct national markets and aligns product prices.
concepts.key_idea: Expanding consumer choice and enabling direct competition between producers located in different nations.
question_patterns: How does foreign trade lead to the integration of markets?
Explain the basic function of foreign trade.
What is the impact of foreign trade on choice and prices of goods?
How do producers in different countries compete through foreign trade?
Describe how import of goods connects markets across nations.

solution_steps.explain: With trade, goods travel from one national market to another, increasing consumer choices.
Prices of similar goods tend to equalize, and distant producers compete directly.

concepts.title: Globalisation
concepts.definition: The rapid process of economic, cultural, and social integration and interconnection among countries worldwide.
concepts.key_idea: Increased cross-border movement of goods, services, technology, capital, and people.
question_patterns: What is globalisation?
Explain the process of rapid integration between countries.
What role do MNCs play in the globalisation process?
How are countries connected besides the movement of goods and services?
What are the key dimensions of globalisation?

solution_steps.explain: MNCs drive integration through foreign trade and foreign investments.
Goods, services, technology, capital, and labor move more freely between nations.

concepts.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in Globalisation
concepts.definition: The application of telecommunications, computers, and internet services to transmit information instantly and coordinate global production.
concepts.key_idea: Enabling real-time communication and remote management of business operations across long distances.
question_patterns: How has technology stimulated the globalisation process?
What role does information technology play in spreading production of services?
Explain how the internet has facilitated global business operations.
Would globalisation have been possible without the expansion of IT?
Describe the link between telecommunications and global integration.

solution_steps.explain: Computers, internet, and satellite communication devices are used to share data.
Designs, orders, and payments are sent instantly across continents, reducing transaction costs.

concepts.title: Liberalisation and Trade Barriers
concepts.section: Liberalisation of foreign trade and foreign investment policy
concepts.definition: The removal of government-imposed restrictions, tariffs, or quotas on imports and exports to facilitate free trade.
concepts.key_idea: Allowing businesses to make independent import-export decisions with minimal state intervention.
question_patterns: What do you understand by liberalisation of foreign trade?
What is a trade barrier and why do governments use them?
Why did the Indian government put barriers to foreign trade after Independence?
What changes in trade policy were made in India starting around 1991?
How does the removal of trade barriers benefit foreign companies?

solution_steps.explain: Trade barriers are restrictions like import taxes or quotas used to regulate foreign trade.
Liberalisation removes these barriers, allowing free entry and exit of goods and investments.

concepts.title: World Trade Organisation (WTO)
concepts.definition: An international body established to formulate rules for global commerce and promote the liberalisation of trade among member nations.
concepts.key_idea: Ensuring free and fair trade globally, though often criticized for power imbalances.
question_patterns: What is the main aim of the World Trade Organisation?
How does the WTO establish rules for international trade?
Why is the WTO criticized by developing countries?
Discuss the debate on trade practices in the agricultural sector under WTO rules.
What is the role of the WTO in global trade liberalisation?

solution_steps.action: Identify the mandate of the WTO
solution_steps.explain: The WTO aims to liberalize international trade by removing barriers and enforcing common rules.
Developed countries sometimes retain barriers while forcing developing nations to remove theirs.

concepts.title: Special Economic Zones (SEZs)
concepts.definition: Designated industrial areas equipped with world-class infrastructure and tax exemptions designed to attract foreign direct investment.
concepts.key_idea: Creating highly favorable localized environments to encourage multinational investments.
question_patterns: What are Special Economic Zones (SEZs)?
Why are central and state governments setting up SEZs in India?
What facilities are provided to companies in Special Economic Zones?
How do SEZs help in attracting foreign investment?
Why has the setting up of SEZs been opposed by some people?

solution_steps.action: Identify the features of an SEZ
solution_steps.explain: SEZs offer world-class infrastructure (electricity, water, roads) and tax holidays for initial years.
The primary goal is to attract foreign multinational corporations to set up manufacturing units.

concepts.title: Fair Globalisation
concepts.section: THE STRUGGLE FOR A FAIR GLOBALISATION
concepts.definition: An inclusive approach to global economic integration that ensures opportunities and benefits are shared equitably among all sections of society.
concepts.key_idea: Balancing market efficiency with social justice and labor rights protection.
question_patterns: What is fair globalisation?
How can the government play a role in ensuring fair globalisation?
Why is there a need for a struggle for fair globalisation?
What steps can be taken to protect small producers and workers in a globalised economy?
How can developing countries negotiate for fairer rules at the WTO?

solution_steps.action: Identify the gaps in current globalisation
solution_steps.explain: Not everyone has benefited; small producers and workers often face job insecurity and losses.
Governments must enforce labor laws, support small producers, and use trade barriers if necessary.

concepts.title: Export Ratio of a Multinational Plant
concepts.definition: The proportion of total production that is exported to foreign markets, expressed as a percentage.
concepts.key_idea: Determining the export orientation of a manufacturing facility relative to its total output.
question_patterns: Calculate the export ratio of the plant given exports and total production.
What percentage of total production was exported by the company?
Find the export percentage of a factory that produces ... units and exports ... units.
Determine the export ratio of an automobile plant.
Calculate how much of the total output is shipped abroad as a percentage.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the export sales by the total production and multiply by 100 to get the percentage.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Ford Motors in India sells {domestic_sales} cars in the domestic market and exports {export_sales} cars to other countries. What is the total production of cars by the plant?

solution_template.action: Sum domestic sales and export sales
solution_template.explain: To find the total production, we add the number of cars sold domestically to the number of cars exported.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A garment manufacturing unit in Ludhiana sells {domestic_sales} footballs locally and exports {export_sales} footballs to European MNCs. Calculate the total production of footballs.

solution_template.action: Sum domestic sales and export sales
solution_template.explain: To find the total production, we add the domestic sales volume to the export sales volume.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A manufacturing plant has a total production of {total_production} units and exports {export_sales} units. Find its export ratio as a percentage.

solution_template.explain: Divide the export sales by the total production and multiply by 100 to get the percentage.

worked_examples.question_pattern: An electronics factory has a total output of {total_production} mobile phones, out of which {export_sales} are exported. Calculate the export ratio of the factory.

solution_template.explain: Divide the export sales by the total production and multiply by 100 to get the percentage.
